intro.title: What Stack32 is
intro.body: Stack32 is a web product for creating and using AI agents in everyday language. You describe a job — research, answer from your docs, draft outreach, summarize notes — and Stack32 assembles an agent that can do that work. You stay in a conversation: create in Build, try in Live, inspect in Structure. There is no workflow editor and no need to pick tools yourself.

lifecycle.title: Three views, one loop
lifecycle.subtitle: Creation, use and clarity live side by side so you never lose the thread.

items.title: Build
items.description: Chat with the Builder like you brief a teammate. Stack32 proposes a first version of your agent, runs a smoke test, and shows progress while it works. Ask for changes — stricter rules, a different tone, a new output format — and it applies them, retests and keeps history.

items.title: Live
items.description: Open a dedicated workspace and talk to your agent as a user would. See steps unfold while it researches, reads sources or drafts. Live is where you validate that the agent actually helps before you rely on it day to day.

items.title: Structure
items.description: Read a clear breakdown of the agent: goal, capabilities, rules and expected output — in human language, not JSON. Structure is how you (and your team) understand what the agent is allowed to do without opening a technical panel.

items.question: How do credits work?
items.answer: Builder credits meter platform model usage when you create or iterate on an agent. They are deducted from real token cost (input + output). On monthly billing the pool resets each month; on annual you get a 12-month pool (e.g. Starter shows 100 credits/month = 1,200 credits/year).

items.question: What’s the difference between monthly and annual?
items.answer: Monthly renews each month (Starter $24, Pro $49, Scale $99 at base). Annual charges 12 months upfront at the reduced rate (20% off): Starter $20, Pro $40, Scale $80 per month equivalent. Credits are always shown as monthly; the usage cap is annualized.

items.question: Can I cancel anytime?
items.answer: Yes. You keep access until the end of the period already paid, then you return to Free. Cancellation does not refund the started period.

items.question: Can I get a refund?
items.answer: Not for a period that has already started: access (Builder credits, agent creation, publishing per plan) activates immediately on payment. By ordering, you accept immediate performance and waive the withdrawal right under the French Consumer Code. See the Refund Policy for very limited exceptions.

items.question: Who handles payment?
items.answer: Billing will be processed securely by Whop. Stack32 never asks you to paste card numbers into a custom form.

items.question: Will prices change?
items.answer: Amounts shown are indicative during beta. If pricing evolves before launch, we communicate clearly before charging differently.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: How Stack32 works, what agents can do, and what to expect before you build your first one.

items.question: Do I need to know how to code?
items.answer: No. Stack32 is designed for non-technical users. You describe the job in plain language; Stack32 builds, tests and runs the agent. You never open a code editor or a node canvas.

items.question: Is this like n8n, Make or Zapier?
items.answer: No. Those tools chain steps on a visual workflow. Stack32 is agent-first: you brief a builder, get something you can chat with immediately, then refine by conversation.

items.question: What is an “agent” here?
items.answer: An agent is a reusable assistant with a clear goal, capabilities (for example web research or your documents), rules and a preferred output style. You create it once, then talk to it whenever you need that job done.

items.question: How is Stack32 different from a generic chatbot?
items.answer: A chatbot answers in the moment. A Stack32 agent is shaped for a specific job, tested as you iterate, inspectable in Structure, and improvable over versions — closer to a teammate than a blank chat window.

items.question: What can my agent do?
items.answer: Typical work includes web research, reading documents you connect, analyzing information, drafting structured text (emails, reports, tables) and following rules you set in Build.

items.question: Can it use my own documents?
items.answer: Yes. You can attach knowledge sources so answers stay grounded in your material, with citations when sources are used. You stay in control of what you upload.

items.question: How long does it take to get a first version?
items.answer: A first working version often appears in under a minute. Most people reach a satisfying result within a few follow-up prompts in Build.

items.question: Can I change an agent after creating it?
items.answer: Yes — that is the core loop. Ask for changes in Build; Stack32 applies them, retests and keeps previous versions so you can evolve safely.

items.question: What languages does the interface support?
items.answer: English and French today. The product is structured so more languages can be added without changing how you build agents.

items.question: How does billing work?
items.answer: A simple monthly subscription for Pro, handled securely by Whop. Free lets you explore with limits. Cancel anytime.

items.question: Who is behind Stack32?
items.answer: Stack32 is a Synko product, operated by Zeldia, a company registered in France.
